evidence_items.publisher: Internal Revenue Service; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence_items.locator: IRS determination letter dated November 3, 2016, opening paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt:
We're pleased to tell you we determined you're exempt from federal income tax
under Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Section 501(c)(3).

evidence_items.explanation: The IRS granted the claimed federal exemption. The letter was included in the California registration package received in August 2017; it does not separately certify safe AI deployment.

evidence_items.publisher: Adler & Colvin, on behalf of OpenAI, Inc.; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence_items.locator: Adler & Colvin registration cover letter, August 24, 2017

receipt.public_excerpt:
We enclose the initial registration of OpenAI, Inc., a Delaware nonprofit nonstock
corporation which qualified to do business in California on January 7,2016, pursuant to
Government Code Section 12585.

evidence_items.explanation: The submission establishes the California registration history and distinguishes it from Delaware incorporation. An initial submission alone does not establish the registry's status in May 2024.

evidence_items.publisher: OpenAI, Inc.; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence_items.locator: 2022 Form 990, Schedule O, response to Part I, line 1

receipt.public_excerpt:
OpenAI’s mission is to build general-purpose artificial intelligence (“AI”) that safely

benefits humanity, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return.

evidence_items.explanation: The latest annual filing publicly available before the post expressly combines safety, humanity's benefit, and freedom from a requirement to generate financial returns. The same return identifies OpenAI, Inc. as exempt under 501(c)(3).

unresolved_gaps: No dated California registry-status record establishing continued registration through May 30, 2024 was retrieved.
The retrieved IRS determination establishes the original exemption, but the evidence package lacks a dated confirmation of its continued status at the post date.
The filings establish the declared safety purpose, but do not show an IRS finding that safe deployment itself was the specific basis for granting or retaining exemption.
